item.title: Calgary mayor floats plebiscite after provincial education property tax increase
item.description: Calgary's mayor made the comments during a special meeting of council called to discuss the potential impact of the provincial budget on Calgarians.

item.title: ‘I’m on medication and running out’: Canadians scramble to leave Middle East
item.description: Global Affairs Canada says more than 100,000 Canadians are registered in the Gulf region, a number that has been growing since Sunday.

item.title: Parents of HUB mall shooting victim push for Canada to change parole eligibility
item.description: If passed, "Brian's Bill" or Bill C-243, would mean those convicted of first- and second-degree murder who are denied parole would have to wait five years to apply again.

item.title: Oak Park Raiders force deciding game with 3-2 OT victory in high school city championship
item.description: The Oak Park Raiders and Vincent Massey Trojans will play a winner take all Game 3 in the championship series on Thursday.

item.title: Meth detention and other health-care issues dominate first day of legislature sitting
item.description: A recently built protective care centre in Winnipeg has started to detain people intoxicated with meth and other drugs for up to 72 hours, Premier Wab Kinew said Wednesday.

item.title: London Knights cut down Guelph Storm 5-2 on Farmer’s Night at Canada Life Place
item.description: Three-point nights from Jaxon Cover and Ryan Brown helped the London Knights to a 5-2 victory over the Guelph Storm on March 4 at Canada Life Place.

item.title: B.C. small businesses suffered worst sales decline in Canada, report states
item.description: The report by Xero Small Business Insights says that small business sales fell 8.2 per cent in B.C., which was double the national average of 4.1 per cent.

item.title: ‘Everything has been a struggle’: More questions from Lapu Lapu victim about donations
item.description: The family of a young man severely injured in the Lapu Lapu Festival tragedy says they are not getting the help or the financial support they expected.

item.title: OpenAI agrees to strengthen safeguards following B.C. mass shooting: minister
